activity.notes: Records Aibak's independent/de facto paramount rule in north India from 1206 to 1210. The Role is phrased as Ruler of Delhi rather than forcing the formal title Sultan because New Cambridge notes numismatic evidence that he may have borne no higher title than malik.

sources.title: Muslim India: the Delhi sultanate — The New Cambridge History of Islam
sources.citation_text: New Cambridge describes Qutb al-Din Aybak's de facto autonomy after 1206, his paramount rule in Muslim India, and his death in 1210, while noting numismatic evidence concerning his formal title.

sources.title: The expansion of Turkic power, 1180–1350 — India before Europe
sources.citation_text: Cambridge treats 1206 as the watershed when Qutb al-Din Aibak seized control of the occupying armies and founded the first Delhi Sultanate dynasty.
